name: Ma Tzŭ-jan
bio: Ma Tzŭ-jan is dated by Giles to the 9th century AD. His poem here is a short fable about a Master and a man content with his lot.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: Ut Melius
poems.author: Ma Tzŭ-jan
poems.text:
In youth I went to study Tag" at its living fountain-head,
And then lay tipsy half the day upon a gilded bed.
"What oaf is this," the Master cried,
"content with human lot?"
And bade me to the world get back and call myself a Sot.
But wherefore seek immortal life by means of wondrous pills?
Noise is not in the market-place, nor quiet on the hills.
The secret of perpetual youth is already known to me:
Accept with philosophic calm whatever fate may be.
